title: Consistency and distributed-systems basics
summary: CAP/PACELC without the folklore, quorums and what they do not guarantee, clocks and ordering, why exactly-once is a property of the whole pipeline, consensus intuition, leases and fencing tokens, and choosing a model for money movement.

units.title: Time, clocks and ordering; exactly-once as an end-to-end property
Consensus, leases, fencing and choosing a model

labs.title: Dynamo-style quorum KV (N, R, W): versions, read repair, sloppy quorums, hinted handoff
Lamport and vector clocks, siblings, and last-write-wins under clock skew
Leader election and log replication intuition (Raft-lite)

outcomes.text: State the CAP theorem correctly (what C, A and P mean, and what it does not say), apply PACELC, and assign a consistency-versus-availability choice to each operation of a banking platform.
Distinguish linearizability, serializability, sequential, causal and eventual consistency and the session guarantees, and identify which anomaly a given system or recorded history permits.
Choose N, R and W for a workload, prove the overlap rule, and explain what quorums do not guarantee: sloppy quorums, partial writes, concurrent writes and non-linearizable reads.
Implement a Dynamo-style quorum key-value coordinator with versioned values, read repair, sloppy quorums and hinted handoff.
Explain why wall-clock last-write-wins loses data under clock skew, quantify the loss, and say what monotonic, hybrid logical and bounded-uncertainty clocks do and do not give.
Implement Lamport and vector clocks, detect concurrent writes, and merge siblings.
Argue that exactly-once is an end-to-end property (at-least-once delivery plus idempotent, deduplicating processing) and place the dedupe record correctly for a given kind of effect.
Explain why consensus needs a majority and how Raft's terms, elections, log matching and commit rule keep committed entries safe.
Design lease-based mutual exclusion with fencing tokens and explain why a lease alone is unsafe.
Choose a consistency model and mechanism for each piece of state in a money-movement system, with numbers, and defend it under follow-up probes.
Implement leader election and log replication as a Raft-style state machine.
Explain hybrid logical clocks and TrueTime-style commit wait, including what happens when one clock in an HLC cluster is far ahead.
